findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses group resource IDs but V1 and callers expect group IDs from resource names
findings.body: In V2, resources for groups are created via getOrCreateResource with name = group.getId() (resolveGroup returns group id as name). The V2 code adds groupResource.getId() (the internal resource UUID) to the granted set, not the group ID. Callers (UsersResource.searchForUser, getUsersCount) pass these IDs to session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS) / getUsersCount, which expect group model IDs. The result is that group-based user filtering never matches, so users visible via view-members/manage-members group permissions are silently excluded.

findings.title: hasPermission looks up group resource by group id as resource name, but V2 resources are named by id too while the all-groups fallback is applied even when a specific resource exists
findings.body: hasPermission(groupId, ...) calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). When the per-group resource is missing, it falls back to the 'Groups' type resource and only checks that some policy exists on it (policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty()), without checking that the policy actually grants the requested scope on that resource before evaluating. Evaluation then proceeds with the type resource; any permission bound to the type resource with any scope from the expected list is accepted. Combined with the missing-resource case for canManage(group) etc., this can grant scopes that the caller only has through unrelated permissions on the all-groups resource. Verify the fallback semantics match Users (which uses the same pattern).

findings.title: policyStore.findByResource called on possibly null resource leads to NPE
findings.body: If AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) returns null (for example the 'Groups' type resource has not been created because the realm admin permission client was initialized before this type existed, or the resource was deleted), resource is null and policyStore.findByResource(server, null) plus resource.getScopes() on the next line will throw NullPointerException rather than denying access. Null-check resource before using it.

findings.title: V2 group permission management methods throw UnsupportedOperationException but are reachable from GroupResource
findings.body: GroupResource.getManagementPermissions and setManagementPermissionsEnabled call AdminPermissions.management(...).groups().isPermissionsEnabled / setPermissionsEnabled / getPermissions / resource(). In V2 these throw UnsupportedOperationException, which results in a 500 rather than a proper error for the management/permissions endpoints when the V2 feature is enabled. Either guard those endpoints or return a meaningful error.

findings.title: canViewMembers in V1 now grants on MANAGE_MEMBERS, changing semantics of requireViewMembers for V1 users
findings.body: canViewMembers was changed to check VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE and MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE and requireViewMembers now delegates to canViewMembers. Previously requireViewMembers used getGroupsWithViewPermission(group), which granted on VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS too, so this is consistent, but the removed per-group method getGroupsWithViewPermission(group) also short-circuited on canView()/canManage() of users; canViewMembers only checks root.users().canView() which in V1 is fine. Verify no behaviour regression for callers that relied on the removed short-circuit for manage role holders.

findings.title: V2 canView/canManage dropped ADMIN role check
findings.body: The change removed AdminRoles.ADMIN from the role checks in canView(user) and canManage(user). Users with the realm 'admin' role (which previously short-circuited) now fall through to permission evaluation and may be denied access to users they previously could see/manage in V2, a regression for admin users. If the removal is intentional it should be explained; otherwise restore it.

findings.title: canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership in V2 now grant via group membership but canMapRoles dropped the canManage(user) delegation
findings.body: canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership previously delegated to canManage(user), which includes manage-permission and group-based manage checks. They now check MANAGE/MAP_ROLES directly and then canManageByGroup, but the group-based check uses canManageMembers, which in V2 also grants via MANAGE_MEMBERS on the group; this widens who can map roles/manage membership via group MANAGE_MEMBERS, which the schema doc does not state. Confirm this is intended.

findings.title: evaluateHierarchy passes method reference to root.groups() evaluated eagerly
findings.body: canManageByGroup uses root.groups()::canManageMembers and canViewByGroup uses root.groups()::canViewMembers. Method reference on root.groups() binds the receiver at evaluation time, which is fine, but canViewByGroup now calls canViewMembers which in V1 checks root.users().canView() per group, causing repeated permission evaluation for each group in the hierarchy (performance cost of N policy evaluations per user in list views).

findings.title: registerListener now only registers when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled at startup
findings.body: The listener registration was moved outside onEvent and guarded by a feature check at registration time. If the profile is evaluated before features are finalized, the listener is never registered and group removal events no longer disable group permissions. Previously the check was performed at event time. Consider keeping the runtime check or documenting startup ordering.

findings.title: getGroups filter no longer short-circuits for users with global group view
findings.body: The filter was changed to stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView) without the prior canViewGlobal precomputation. canView(GroupModel) calls canView() on every element, re-evaluating role checks and policy evaluation per group, which is a performance regression for large group lists.

findings.title: getSubGroups filter re-evaluates global canView per subgroup
findings.body: The previous code computed canViewGlobal once and reused it; the new filter(auth.groups()::canView) calls canView(GroupModel) for each subgroup, which in V2 performs policy evaluation per element. This is an unnecessary per-item cost.

findings.title: Double semicolon in field declaration
findings.body: The field declaration 'new GroupRepresentation();;' has a stray extra semicolon. Minor, but it should be cleaned up.

findings.title: testManageGroupMembership has no assertion on the joinGroup result and relies on silent success
findings.body: The final joinGroup call is not wrapped with any assertion that membership was actually created; a silently no-op call would still pass. Verify bob is a member of topGroup afterwards.

findings.title: testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers does not cover view-by-all-groups or negative cases for group VIEW_MEMBERS
findings.body: The test only checks positive VIEW_MEMBERS on the single group. There is no negative test showing a user outside the group remains invisible when only VIEW_MEMBERS on a different group exists, nor a test for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returning the correct group IDs (which the V2 implementation gets wrong).
